speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: asked the Minister for Education (Schools) whether it is feasible to scan or digitise examination scripts before sending them to Cambridge Assessment in the United Kingdom for marking so as to better deal with incidents of scripts being misplaced or stolen.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Education (Schools))
text: This includes a full scrutiny of the courier services offered by its suppliers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Education (Schools))
text: However, given the large volume of answer scripts and number of subject papers offered each year, the implementation of the scanning and electronic marking of answer scripts would have to be carefully considered.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: The option of allowing a re-sit can be understood as being fair.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: It was a full examination and these were candidates that did not have the opportunity to have their submissions marked.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: The issue, I suppose, is really to look at those candidates who had a presumptive grade assigned.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: If you look at that subset, the technique that was used is something that has been used and the model has been developed quite robustly.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: One can imagine that, on a regular basis every year, there are candidates who, through illnesses or unfortunate circumstances, are unable to submit every component of an exam.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: In this case, it is only one out of four components of the exam which went missing.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: This is something we have developed over time.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: The three bodies involved did their analyses on this occasion and also backchecked the analyses with respect to the outcome for these candidates.
